body.statement:
Let \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_m\) be independent, centered random variables satisfying \(|Z_j|\leq M\), and put \(v=\sum_{j=1}^m E Z_j^2\).  For every \(x>0\),
\[
 P\!\left(\left|\sum_{j=1}^m Z_j\right|\geq \sqrt{2vx}+\frac{Mx}{3}\right)\leq 2e^{-x}.
\]

source.verbatim_statement: Theorem 2.10 (Bernstein inequality). Let X_1,…,X_n be independent real-valued random variables. Assume that there exist positive numbers v and c such that ∑ E[X_i²] ≤ v and ∑ E[(X_i)_+^q] ≤ (q!/2)vc^(q−2) for all integers q ≥ 3. If S = ∑(X_i−E X_i), then, in particular, for all t > 0, P{S ≥ √(2vt)+ct} ≤ e^(−t).

attestation.note: Verified in the complete book PDF hosted by the Higher School of Economics, p. 37. Applying the theorem to both Z_i and −Z_i, with c=M/3 (the bounded moment condition follows from |Z_i|≤M), and taking a union bound gives exactly the two-sided form recorded in the node.
